newsitem.title: FRANCE: Guatemala offers Centam meeting for Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala offers Centam meeting for Chirac.

text.p: Guatemalan President Alvaro Arzu, visiting Paris to receive the UNESCO peace prize, on Wednesday offered to host a meeting of Central American leaders if French President Jacques Chirac accepts his invitation to visit.
"We hope President Chirac will soon visit Guatemala. In that case I will arrange for a meeting with all our Central American counterparts," Arzu told reporters after calling on Chirac.
Chirac, who toured six South American countries last March and has vowed to visit all of Latin America, reaffirmed he would keep working to develop links between the region and Europe.

Arzu and Guatemalan guerrilla leader Rolando Moran are to receive on Thursday the Houphouet-Boigny peace prize awarded by the United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organisation for ending more than three decades of bloodshed in the Central American state.

"This is an honour because it is an extremely important prize which I will, of course, accept in the name of the Guatemalan people," Arzu told reporters. "It was the people who achieved the victory in reaching a peace accord."

UNESCO announced in January that it was awarding its annual peace prize jointly to Arzu and Moran for signing last December a peace accord resolving a 36-year guerrilla uprising during which some 140,000 people were killed or "disappeared".
